title: The Temple of Atal'Hakkar
body: The Temple of Atal'Hakkar is the great shrine the Atal'ai trolls raised to their blood god Hakkar, the temple the green dragonflight drowned beneath the Pool of Tears. It did not fall to ruin under the water. Its halls still stand, ring upon ring, sinking level by level toward a deep round pit at the bottom, and the Atal'ai still hold the upper rings: warriors and witch doctors, priests and their slaves, and dead trolls of the tribe who have not stopped serving it. Below them the dragonkin of the green flight keep watch in the middle halls, and they have no welcome for anyone who comes in. The lowest halls lie flooded with ooze, where slimes, maggots and lurkers crawl through the muck. Explorers come for the trolls' relics and for the secrets of the temple's halls, others come to strike at the Atal'ai before their god returns, and a few come on errands for masters far away, after something only the temple holds.

title: The Hall of the Cursed
body: The upper ring of the temple is the Hall of the Cursed, a chain of chambers circling the great well at its heart, and the Atal'ai hold it. Warriors stand watch in every chamber beside witch doctors who hurl lightning, hex their foes and heal their kin, and who run for help when the fight turns against them. Corpse eaters crouch among them, trolls who feed on the dead, and unliving Atal'ai, dead trolls still in the tribe's service, fly into a frenzy when they are badly hurt. Slaves of the Atal'ai are kept in the chambers under their masters' eyes.

title: The Pit of Refuse
body: At the very bottom of the temple lies the Pit of Refuse, a deep round chamber whose floor is drowned in ooze. Saturated oozes heave through the muck and throw off smaller oozes as they fight, while murk worms, slime maggots and deep lurkers crawl the flooded floor and the passages around it. Around the rim of the pit rise six balconies, each holding a great serpent statue at its edge. Near the way into the room an ancient altar stands silent, and the serpents carved on it look much like the statues above.

title: The Pit of Sacrifice
body: At the heart of the temple a great well drops through its middle halls, the Pit of Sacrifice. On its floor the dragonkin of the green flight keep their watch among whelps of their kind. Above them, on six ledges that overlook the pit, stand six champions of the Atal'ai, each alone on his own ledge. They are dead trolls who still fight for their tribe, and each is a power in his own right. Whatever the Atal'ai keep beyond the pit, these six stand watch over it.

parts.body: Zolo was the shaman of the six. He loosed lightning that leapt from one foe to the next and planted a totem from which skeletons of the Atal'ai rose to fight for him, until he fell on his ledge.

title: Jammal'an the Prophet
body: Jammal'an the Prophet leads the Atal'ai from the Lair of the Chosen, the sanctum where the tribe's deathwalkers, mummified dead and high priests keep watch, and he waits there with green power streaming about him. A shield of force barred the way to him while the six champions of the pit still stood. When the last of them fell he cried out to his people that the shield was down and called the Atal'ai to rise up. Ogom the Wretched, a dead troll, stands at the prophet's side, and the whole lair answers when the prophet calls. Here he stands to defend the vision that drives his tribe.

parts.body: Jammal'an met his foes crying that the Soulflayer comes, and his lair came with him. He set totems that seized foes in the earth, called down pillars of flame and mended his people with waves of healing. Worst was his hex: he turned his foes' own companions against them, crying Join us. Near the end he cried that Hakkar would live again. He fell all the same, and with him his hex was broken.

title: The Lair of the Chosen
body: The Lair of the Chosen is the holiest of the Atal'ai halls, the sanctum of their prophet in the middle reaches of the temple. Its keepers are the tribe's dead and its priests. Atal'ai deathwalkers lay shadowy pain on their foes and send them fleeing in terror, and when one falls its spirit rises from the body to fight on. Mummified Atal'ai spread a fevered plague, priests and high priests heal their kin, wrap themselves in shields of shadow and call up skeletons to their side, and at the far end of the hall the prophet waits.

title: The Shade of Eranikus
body: In the Chamber of the Dreamer lies the shade of Eranikus, a great dragon of the green flight. Near him stands a font, and the dragons Morphaz and Hazzas keep the passage that leads to him. While the prophet of the Atal'ai lived, the shade lay out of reach of every blade and spell, as if not wholly in this world. Only when the prophet fell did the dragon stir and become a foe that could be fought, and the green dragonkin of the temple answer to him.

parts.body: Eranikus rose crying that this evil could not be allowed to enter this world, and he called his children to him. The dragonkin still alive in the temple came to his call. He shook the ground with stomps that staggered his foes, breathed acid over them and cast them into a deep slumber, until at last the shade fell in his chamber.

title: The Green Wardens
body: The middle halls of the temple belong to the dragonkin of the green flight, who hold the floor of the great pit and the passages around it. Scalebanes stand guard behind their shields, wanderers strike at the joints of their foes' armor, wyrmkin spit acid and lull their enemies to sleep, and whelps of the flight swarm about the floor of the pit. They do not side with the Atal'ai, yet they turn on every outsider who comes down into their halls as fiercely as the trolls do.

parts.body: When the prophet of the Atal'ai fell, two drakes appeared in the Pit of Sacrifice, Dreamscythe and Weaver. Dreamscythe had a warning for those who had slain the prophet: they knew not what they did, and the dragons must destroy them for their own good. Then he came at them crying Turn back, do not wake the dreamer, beating his wings to hurl them back and breathing acid on them, until he fell.

title: The Avatar of Hakkar
body: The Avatar of Hakkar is the form in which the blood god can enter the world, and the Sanctum of the Fallen God, deep in the temple, is where it can be called forth. There the dead god can be stirred, and he will send his minions against whoever wakes him. His bloodkeepers carry Hakkari blood, and with it the eternal flames that hold Hakkar's spirit can be doused. When every flame is out, the avatar enters the world, and there it must be faced and defeated.

parts.body: When the rite began, the shade of Hakkar rose in the middle of the sanctum, and circles of summoning burned about it, spilling out minions of the god. Bloodkeepers came, and dragonkin of the green flight came crying out against the summoning and bent their magic on the shade to smother it. As each eternal flame was doused with Hakkari blood, the shade's voice grew: it drew closer to the world, it tasted the blood of life, it was here. At the last it roared that Hakkar lives.

parts.body: Then the avatar came forth and fell on those who had called it, crying death to mortals. It lashed at those before it, laid a curse on their tongues that slowed their spells and drove one of them after another into madness, so that they turned on their own companions. For all that, the avatar was brought down in the sanctum, and the god's shape in the world was broken.

title: The Circle of Statues
body: In the Sunken Temple the goblin Marvon Rivetseeker once stumbled through a great round room full of serpent statues, the room he remembers so dimly. He has become sure that the circle holds a secret, though the room is as dangerous as it is strange, and that the secret is worth the risk of finding it. Now he sends those bold enough back into the temple in his place, down to that room, to learn what its serpent statues and the altar among them are hiding.

parts.body: Marvon put his faith in the altar. Lying on the ledge after the trap that nearly killed him, he had looked down on it, and he believed it was the key. He handed over the stone circle and asked that it be brought to the altar of Hakkar.
sources: quest 3446 description (I think that this altar is the secret; bring this token to the altar)
item 10466 Atal'ai Stone Circle (3446's source item)

parts.body: In the side of the altar was a hollow just the size of Marvon's stone. Pushed into it, the stone circle locked into place with a sound, and the altar seemed to be waiting for whatever came next, as though it had more to show to anyone who studied it closely.
sources: quest 3446 completion and reward texts (a depression in its side just the size of the token; it locks into place; perhaps you should examine this altar further)

gameobject 148836 Altar of Hakkar, ender of 3446; gossip 1288 option (How could the altar and the statues be related) shown only once 3446 is rewarded (conditions 15/1288), opening npc_text 1935 and a script that lights six small lights in turn

parts.body: Marvon remembered more. From the main altar he had once set off a series of lights, one after another, and he believed that whoever understood what they meant could unlock what the room was hiding. He warned, though, that a great evil dwells in the temple, and that anything of value there would be fiercely guarded.
sources: quest 3447 description (from the main altar I was able to activate a series of lights; uncover what these lights mean; great evil lies in the temple; anything valuable will be fervently guarded)

parts.body: The statues had to be woken in the right order. Each one touched in its turn lit up with a great light, while one touched out of turn lashed out with poison, dark energy or flame. When the sixth was lit, an idol of Hakkar rose in the middle of the pit, and with it its guardian, Atal'alarion, a towering troll who cried that his banishment was ended and the blood should flow.
sources: smart_scripts 148830-148835 with conditions 22 (sourcegroup 1: in order, set instance data 10 and summon light 148937; sourcegroup 4: out of order, cast Atal'ai Poison 18949, Dark Energy 18948 or Flame of Hakkar 12354)

parts.body: Atal'alarion came on promising to feast on the bones of those who had woken him. He swept them aside with great slams and shook the floor of the pit beneath their feet, but he fell at last before the idol he was set to guard.

parts.body: With the guardian dead, the idol could be studied. Its eye glittered brightly even in the half darkness of the temple, and it was clear enough to show something shining behind it. Slid aside, it gave up what the statue held: the treasure of the Atal'ai, the secret of the circle at last.

title: Malfurion Stormrage
body: In the Chamber of the Dreamer the walls trembled, and Malfurion Stormrage appeared to the champion who had come in search of the green shard of the scepter. He knew why the champion had come and what they sought, and he warned that Eranikus would not give up the shard freely, for the dragon had been twisted by the same force the champion had set out to destroy. Even within the Dream, he said, an Old God's power could reach.

parts.body: The way he gave was a hard one. Eranikus, now a tyrant of the Dream, longed to be brought into Azeroth, where he would stop at nothing to destroy Malfurion's body, and yet only so could the shard be won. Malfurion called it a journey of redemption: the shard recovered and Eranikus cleansed of the Old Gods' taint. He sent the champion to an agent waiting outside Darnassus, who would tell Tyrande without alerting Staghelm, and sighed over a fall from grace a thousand years in the making.
sources: creature_text 15362 group 3 (Eranikus wants nothing more than to be brought to Azeroth from the Dream; he will stop at nothing to destroy my physical manifestation; the only way to recover the scepter shard) and group 4 (You will bring him back into this world)

quest 8733 description (a journey of redemption; recover the green scepter shard; cleanse Eranikus of the taint placed upon him by the Old Gods; one of my agents outside the walls of Darnassus; inform Tyrande without alerting Staghelm; A fall from grace a thousand years in the making)
